question: What is the UK National Living Wage hourly rate for workers aged 21 and over from April 2026?
answer:
The UK National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026, up from £12.21 [1][2]. That is a 50p (4.1%) increase, and the Government accepted the Low Pay Commission's recommendations in full [2]. The rate was set by amendment to regulation 4 of the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015, which extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland [6]. Workers in their first year of an apprenticeship are not covered by the NLW and are on the apprentice rate instead [1].

keyPoints.text: The National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026.
The rate rose by 50p (4.1%) from the previous £12.21 rate that applied until 31 March 2026.
The increase was set by the Low Pay Commission's recommendations and accepted in full by the Government.
Regulations bringing the £12.71 rate into force from 1 April 2026 replace the £12.21 figure in the 2015 Regulations.

mayBeStale.text: The £12.21 figure from the 2025 rate is superseded and no longer applies after 31 March 2026.
The Low Pay Commission's 2027 projections (around £13.18 central estimate) are forecasts, not the current rate.
